items.prompt: Slide the white rook up the d-file as far as it can go in one move. (The kings only fill the position.)

claims.statement: The rook can go from d4 to d5.
The rook cannot land on d6, where its own pawn stands.
The rook cannot jump over its own pawn to d8.

hints: Look straight up from the rook, one square at a time.
The d-file has a white pawn on d6. Can the rook go onto a square held by its own pawn?
The rook stops on the square just before its own pawn.
items.explain: The rook slides up the d-file to d5. Its own pawn on d6 stops it one square short: it cannot land there and cannot jump over it.

feedback_by_move.d4d3: That goes down the file, away from the pawn. The task was to go up as far as possible; the rook can only reach d5 in that direction.
feedback_by_move.d4h4: That slides along the fourth rank. Up the file, the farthest square is d5.

items.prompt: White to move. The piece on f3 is a rook. Tap every square it can move to. (Go one direction at a time, from the rook outward.)

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the rook on f3 can move to.
The piece on f3 is a white rook.
A black pawn stands on f7.

hints: Start upward from f3 and walk square by square until you meet a piece.
Downwards, your own pawn on f2 is the first piece. Along the rank, nothing stands in the way on either side.
Up the file the rook may take the black pawn on f7 and stops there. The black queen on c4 is off every line of the rook.
items.explain: Up the file: f4, f5, f6 and the black pawn on f7, which the rook may take. Down: its own pawn on f2 is the first piece, so nothing. Left along the rank: e3 to a3. Right: g3 and h3. The queen on c4 is on none of the rook's lines.

items.prompt: White to move. Take the black knight with the rook. (Which line leads to it, and is anything in between?)

claims.statement: The rook can go from h1 to h5.
A black knight stands on h5.
The rook cannot go past the knight to h8.

hints: Find the black knight, then see which of the rook's lines it is on.
It is on the h-file. The squares h2, h3 and h4 are empty.
The first enemy piece on the file is the knight, so the rook can slide to h5 and take it.
items.explain: The knight is the first piece on the h-file, with h2, h3 and h4 empty in between. The rook slides up and takes it on h5, where the slide ends.

feedback_by_move.h1h4: That is a legal square, one short of the knight. The rook stops beside it and takes nothing.
feedback_by_move.h1g1: That slides sideways along the first rank. The knight is not on that line.

items.prompt: White to move. Can the rook on b2 reach b8 in ONE move?

claims.statement: The rook cannot go from b2 to b8 in one move.
A white bishop stands on b6, on the same file.

hints: Name the piece on b2, then look up its file.
Is every square between b2 and b8 empty?
Your own bishop stands on b6, between the rook and b8.
items.explain: No. The white bishop on b6 is on the b-file between the rook and b8. A rook cannot jump over its own piece.

items.prompt: Same position. What is the fewest number of rook moves that takes it from b2 to b8?

claims.statement: One move is not enough.
After the rook steps to c2, it attacks the whole c-file up to c8 (and the second rank).

hints: One move is blocked. Look for a different file that reaches the top row.
The bishop blocks the b-file only. Which neighbouring file is clear all the way up?
Step sideways to c2 first, then slide up the clear c-file.
items.explain: Two moves. The bishop blocks the b-file, so the rook sidesteps to the clear c-file and then slides all the way up. One blocker cost one extra move.

items.prompt: White to move. The rook can slide up the e-file only so far. Tap the one piece that ends that slide.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the rook on e1 can move to: the e-file stops at e5.
The piece on e5 is a black knight.
The rook cannot reach e8.

hints: Think about which of the rook's lines points toward the top of the board.
Squares e2, e3 and e4 are empty. The white knight on c4 is beside the file, not on it.
The first piece on the file, going up, is the black knight on e5.
items.explain: The black knight on e5 is the first piece on the e-file. The rook may take it but cannot pass. The other pieces (the pawns, the white knight on c4) are off the file and block nothing.

items.prompt: White to move. What can the piece on a1 do?

options: it can only move up the file
it can only move along the rank

claims.statement: The piece on a1 has no legal destination.
The piece on a1 is a white rook.

hints: Name the piece on a1, then look at the squares next to it on its two lines.
A rook in a corner has only two lines.
Both neighbours, a2 and b1, hold white pieces.
items.explain: No. The rook is a rook, but its pawn stands on a2 and its bishop on b1. Both are its own pieces, so it has no move until one of them goes.

items.prompt: White to move. Tap every square the piece on c3 can move to.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the piece on c3 can move to.
The piece on c3 is a white bishop.

hints: First decide what kind of piece it is.
A bishop travels on diagonals. Walk each of the four diagonals until something stops you.
One diagonal is blocked at once by its own pawn on b2; another ends with an enemy pawn on d4.
items.explain: It is a bishop, so it uses diagonals. Up-left: b4, a5. Up-right: the black pawn on d4, which it may take. Down-left: its own pawn on b2 blocks. Down-right: d2 and e1.

items.prompt: Black to move. Tap every square the piece on d8 can move to.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the piece on d8 can move to.
The piece on d8 is a black rook.

hints: Name the piece first. Then take the four directions one at a time.
Down the d-file the first piece is Black's own pawn on d5. Along the eighth rank, the king stands on g8.
Down: d7 and d6. Left: c8, b8, a8. Right: e8 and f8.
items.explain: A black rook. Down the file it reaches d7 and d6, then its own pawn on d5 stops it. Along the rank it reaches a8, b8, c8 on the left and e8, f8 on the right; its own king on g8 ends that line.

items.prompt: White to move. One move takes a black piece for nothing in return. Find it.

claims.statement: The rook can go from b1 to b4.
The bishop on b4 is attacked and no black piece defends it.

hints: Look at each black piece and ask which of White's lines reaches it.
The black bishop is on the same file as your rook.
b2 and b3 are empty, so the rook can slide up to b4 and take it.
items.explain: The rook slides up the b-file through the empty b2 and b3 and takes the bishop on b4. No black piece defends the bishop.
